I couldn't do this research. My tools stopped working before I could read a single page. My first attempt to open several commentary pages at once hit the server's usage limit, and the system then blocked any further tool calls for this turn. So I have no source material for Isaiah 2.

You asked me to report only what the pages actually say, cite a URL for every point and not fill gaps from my own knowledge. That means I can't write any verse notes yet, so I haven't written any.

These are the pages I tried to open and will read first when the tools are available again:

- **Verse-by-verse commentary:**
  - Enduring Word: https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/isaiah-2/
  - Ellicott: https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/isaiah/2.htm
  - Gill: https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/isaiah/2.htm
  - Pulpit Commentary: https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/isaiah/2.htm
  - Barnes: https://biblehub.com/commentaries/barnes/isaiah/2.htm
  - JFB: https://biblehub.com/commentaries/jfb/isaiah/2.htm
  - Precept Austin: https://www.preceptaustin.org/isaiah-2-commentary
- **Modern scholarship:** the NET Bible notes at https://netbible.org/bible/Isaiah+2
- **Searches I still need to run:**
  - Where Protestant traditions differ on verses 2–4: when "the last days" happen and whether the passage points to the church or a future kingdom on earth. I'd check Ligonier, Desiring God, GTY, the Wesley Center, AG and LCMS.
  - The swords-into-plowshares verse and the "do not forgive them" line in verse 9.
  - Catholic and Orthodox readings at New Advent (Church Fathers) and OCA.
  - Bible Odyssey articles on the passage, including how it relates to Micah 4.

If you ask again in a new message, I'll open these pages one or two at a time so I don't hit the limit. Then I'll write the notes verse by verse with a URL after each point.
